leads.title: Psalm 86, a prayer of David; there is none like you among the gods ↔ The Opening (al-Fatiha)
leads.summary: 2 correspondences read side by side: 2 shared wording.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/01-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: God called al-Rahman and al-Rahim (the Merciful, the Compassionate), paired names from the root r-h-m (womb, mercy) (weight 7.1); Prayer to be guided on the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim) (weight 6.8). Pair score 13.9.

Only in Psalm 86, a prayer of David; there is none like you among the gods: God delivered the speaker's soul from the lowest Sheol (she'ol tahtiyyah); Prayer 'Unite my heart to fear your name'; Elias (Ilyas) rebukes his people: 'Will you call on Ba'l and forsake the best of creators?'; Petitioner asks God for a sign of favor so his enemies may see and be ashamed; Petitioner calls himself 'the son of your handmaid'; All flesh, or all nations, come to God to pray or worship; Individual lament: a sufferer complains of enemies or distress, petitions God and vows praise; Formula of divine attributes: slow to anger, abundant in mercy, visits iniquity to fourth generation; 'Who is like you among the gods, YHWH?'.

Only in The Opening (al-Fatiha): Text or act opened with the formula 'In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate'; Three ways contrasted: those God favored, those under wrath, and those gone astray; Communal confession 'You alone we worship, you alone we ask for help'; Praise (hamd) belongs to God, Lord of the worlds (rabb al-alamin); Contrast of the way of the righteous, which God knows, and the way of the wicked, which perishes [divergence between the texts]; God is king or master of the Day of Judgment (yawm al-din); Contrast of the way of the righteous, which God knows, and the way of the wicked, which perishes.

matches.note: Ps 86:15 ʾēl raḥûm wĕ-ḥannûn ʾerek ʾappayim: raḥûm is one adjective in the attribute formula; Q 1:1, 1:3 ar-raḥmān ar-raḥīm: two r-ḥ-m forms paired as names, opening the text. Same root, the formula's adjective made into a pair of titles.
